# Billing System Migration Rollout Plan
**40,000 users | Old + new systems running in parallel**

## Overview

Migration proceeds in four named phases, moving from internal validation through to full cutover, with the old system kept alive as a fallback well past the final user batch. Each phase gates on explicit entry criteria measured against the previous phase's results, not on calendar time.

---

## Phase 1: Canary (0.25% — ~100 users)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed end-to-end reconciliation testing in staging against a mirrored production dataset, with 100% invoice-amount parity on 10,000 synthetic test accounts, and rollback tooling (re-pointing a user back to the old system) has been tested successfully at least 5 times.

**Population:** Internal employee accounts and consenting volunteer customers (mix of plan types) — not real-money-sensitive customers.

**Activities:** Dual-write/dual-run both systems for this cohort; compare invoices, payment postings, and dunning events line-by-line. Manual review of every discrepancy.

**Duration:** Minimum 2 full billing cycles before advancing.

---

## Phase 2: Early Adopters (5% — ~2,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completed 2 full billing cycles with zero unresolved financial discrepancies (see halt metric below) and support ticket volume from migrated users did not exceed 1.5x the baseline rate for non-migrated users.

**Population:** Randomly sampled across plan tiers and geographies, excluding enterprise/high-ARR accounts and any account currently in an active dispute or dunning cycle.

**Activities:** Continue parallel-run reconciliation but shift to automated diffing with human review only on flagged exceptions. Begin monitoring customer-facing symptoms (failed payments, duplicate charges) via support and payment-gateway webhooks, not just backend logs.

**Duration:** Minimum 1 full billing cycle before advancing.

---

## Phase 3: General Availability Ramp (35% — ~14,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 sustained a payment failure delta of less than 0.1 percentage points versus the old-system control group for a full billing cycle, and finance has signed off on ledger reconciliation for all Phase 1–2 migrated accounts.

**Population:** Broad rollout by cohort (e.g., billing-anniversary date buckets) to spread cutover load evenly across the month; enterprise and high-ARR accounts still excluded and migrated only in Phase 4 with dedicated white-glove support.

**Activities:** Reduce dual-write reconciliation sampling to a statistical subset (e.g., 10% of transactions) rather than full parity checking, given volume. Automated anomaly alerting becomes primary detection mechanism.

**Duration:** Minimum 1 full billing cycle before advancing.

---

## Phase 4: Full Cutover — Final Batch (59.75% — ~23,900 users, including all remaining and enterprise accounts)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 3 held the halt-metric thresholds below their limits for two consecutive billing cycles, enterprise account contacts have been individually notified at least 30 days in advance, and a dedicated incident-response rotation is staffed for the cutover window.

**Population:** All remaining users, including enterprise/high-ARR accounts.

**Activities:** Migrate remaining users in scheduled sub-waves by billing-anniversary date. The old system remains fully operational in read/fallback mode for at least one full billing cycle after the last user is migrated, to handle late-arriving disputes, chargebacks, and reconciliation of the final cycle billed on the old system. Decommissioning the old system is explicitly **out of scope for this plan** and must be a separate, subsequent phase gated on its own criteria (e.g., zero fallback invocations for 60 days, completed financial audit of the full migration).

---

## Halt / Rollback Metrics

Roll back the current phase and freeze further migration immediately if, at any point during a phase:

- **Payment failure rate** for migrated users exceeds **2% above** the concurrent baseline failure rate on the old system, measured over any rolling 24-hour window.
- **Invoice amount discrepancy** (new system vs. expected/reconciled amount) is detected on more than **0.5%** of invoices in any billing run.
- **Duplicate charge incidents** exceed **5 confirmed cases** in any 24-hour period, regardless of percentage.

Any single trigger pauses new migrations into the current phase; already-migrated users are not automatically rolled back but are placed under enhanced monitoring pending root-cause analysis.

---

## Risks

RISK: Duplicate or missed charges during dual-run window due to both systems attempting to bill the same invoice | Implement a single source-of-truth billing-lock flag per account so only one system is authoritative for charge execution at any time, with automated reconciliation alerts on conflicts | Payments Engineering Lead
RISK: Data drift between old and new customer/plan records causes incorrect pricing after migration | Run automated nightly parity checks on plan, pricing, and entitlement data between both systems throughout all phases, blocking migration of any account with an unresolved diff | Data Integrity Team
RISK: Enterprise customers experience invoice format or payment terms changes that breach contractual SLAs | Migrate enterprise accounts only in the final phase with individualized pre-migration review and 30-day advance notice, plus a dedicated account manager check-in | Enterprise Customer Success Lead
RISK: Support team is overwhelmed by migration-related tickets, delaying detection of real financial issues | Stand up a dedicated migration support queue with escalation paths and staff it proportionally to each phase's user count before that phase begins | Customer Support Operations Manager
RISK: Rollback path itself is broken or untested when actually needed under production load | Require a successful rollback drill (with real traffic shadowing) as an explicit gate before advancing out of Phase 1, and re-test rollback tooling before each subsequent phase | Site Reliability Engineering Lead

PHASES: 4
